primaryStory.title: Campaign-scale reliability-gated feedback
primaryStory.headline: InvDesMobility converts first-principles mobility validation into reliability-gated feedback for closed-loop inverse design of two-dimensional semiconductors.
primaryStory.summary: InvDesMobility packages first-principles mobility calculations into reliability-gated feedback for inverse design of two-dimensional semiconductors. This snapshot connects 516 seed structures, 2,064 seed carrier-direction channels, a 2.4 million-structure generated campaign, 102 DFT candidates, 41 retained generated formulas, and 659 total retained feedback labels.
primaryStory.abstract: In closed-loop computational discovery, first-principles calculations increasingly update generative and acquisition models, not only validate final candidates. For multi-stage density functional theory workflows, the bottleneck is feedback admissibility: deciding which completed calculations are reliable enough to shape subsequent search. We present InvDesMobility, a closed-loop framework that turns first-principles mobility calculations into auditable feedback for inverse design of two-dimensional semiconductors. The framework evaluates 2,064 carrier--direction channels from 516 seed semiconductors and retains 573 reliability-gated entries across 280 materials. These retained entries train a structure-aware graph neural network for candidate prioritization, recovering 8 of 28 true top-decile seed materials within the predicted top 10\%, corresponding to a 2.9-fold enrichment. Across multiple iterations, the loop screens 2.4 million generated structures, validates 102 candidates by DFT and retains 41 generated formulas with 86 reliability-gated channels. The study converts multi-stage first-principles validation into reusable, state-traceable feedback for autonomous materials discovery.

chunks.title: Abstract
chunks.text: In closed-loop computational discovery, first-principles calculations increasingly update generative and acquisition models, not only validate final candidates. For multi-stage density functional theory workflows, the bottleneck is feedback admissibility: deciding which completed calculations are reliable enough to shape subsequent search. We present InvDesMobility, a closed-loop framework that turns first-principles mobility calculations into auditable feedback for inverse design of two-dimensional semiconductors. The framework evaluates 2,064 carrier-direction channels from 516 seed semiconductors and retains 573 reliability-gated entries across 280 materials. These retained entries train a structure-aware graph neural network for candidate prioritization, recovering 8 of 28 true top-decile seed materials within the predicted top 10\

chunks.title: Introduction
chunks.text: Closed-loop computational discovery increasingly couples generative models, acquisition functions and physics-based simulations into iterative search processes . In these systems, a simulation result is no longer a passive endpoint: once returned to training or acquisition, it becomes a decision signal that shapes subsequent search. This change creates a validation problem distinct from throughput. For properties assembled through multi-stage density functional theory (DFT) workflows, a calculation can converge and yield a finite scalar while still being too fragile to reuse as feedback. The central bottleneck is therefore feedback admissibility: determining which completed calculations are reliable enough to re-enter the learning loop as qualified evidence. We use carrier mobility in two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors as a stringent test case for this problem. These materials are attractive for electronic and optoelectronic devices because of their atomically thin geometry, electrostatic tunability and anisotropic transport , and transistor studies show why mobility, contact effects and benchmarking reliability remain central .

chunks.title: Introduction
chunks.text: For closed-loop learning, mobility is useful precisely because it turns many intermediate physical quantities into a single apparently simple scalar. In the deformation-potential workflow used here, a reported channel mobility is assembled from band-edge identity, effective masses, strain-dependent band-edge shifts, two-dimensional elastic response and an assumed phonon-scattering model. Small failures-band-edge switching, unstable effective-mass fitting, poorly conditioned response fits or scattering assumptions outside their range of validity -can produce finite values with ambiguous epistemic status. In an anisotropic 2D material, the relevant feedback unit is therefore not a material-level label, but an auditable carrier-direction channel. Recent progress has strengthened several components of closed-loop materials design, but these capabilities do not by themselves decide whether an assembled first-principles property should update a learning system.

chunks.title: Introduction
chunks.text: Materials databases and high-throughput infrastructures provide reference sets , machine-learning and active-learning models enable rapid ranking , and diffusion- or flow-based generators propose extensive candidate pools . Provenance-aware workflow systems and autonomous laboratories make scientific campaigns more reproducible and stateful . If mobility validation is postponed to the end of a campaign, expensive calculations do not inform generator adaptation or acquisition ranking. Conversely, if every converged or finite mobility value is admitted into training, the loop can learn from unstable fits, band-edge switches or ill-conditioned response parameters. Reliable closed-loop design therefore requires that numerical output, cautionary evidence and retained feedback be separated before they influence the search process. To address this problem, we develop InvDesMobility, a multi-agent closed-loop framework for inverse design of 2D semiconductors built around a first-principles mobility feedback engine.

chunks.title: Introduction
chunks.text: Drawing on agentic scientific workflows, provenance-aware workflow systems and retrieval-augmented decision support , InvDesMobility coordinates a VASP-based mobility workflow across planning, execution, validation and recovery. It maintains relaxed-structure feedback, channel-resolved mobility feedback and acquisition ranking as separate state objects, records provenance and uncertainty, and assigns feedback status through explicit reliability criteria. The agent layer does not replace first-principles physics or turn acquisition scores into transport results; it keeps a multi-stage calculation traceable and auditable enough that only qualified outcomes become learning signals. More broadly, the framework treats reliability as a first-class variable for integrating complex first-principles property evaluations into autonomous discovery systems. We evaluate this design in a closed-loop campaign that starts from 516 2DMatPedia-derived seed semiconductors and completes multiple feedback iterations .

chunks.title: Results
chunks.text: We evaluate InvDesMobility through four linked tests: whether the runtime turns multi-stage mobility calculations into auditable feedback, whether the seed set yields reliability-gated channel entries rather than unqualified scalar labels, whether these entries support acquisition enrichment rather than stand-alone mobility prediction, and whether the same feedback contract can be maintained across generated candidates. Unless specified otherwise, a retained feedback entry denotes a carrier-direction channel that passes the stated reliability criteria; non-retained outputs remain part of the audit record rather than entering the learning loop.

chunks.title: InvDesMobility framework
chunks.text: We first test the runtime contract used throughout the campaign. InvDesMobility connects seed mobility construction, structure generation, physical screening, acquisition ranking, first-principles validation and feedback assignment into one design loop (Fig. a). Seed and generated 2D semiconductors are evaluated by the same stateful mobility engine. Quality-controlled relaxed structures update the DiffCSP/InvDesFlow generator, retained channel-resolved mobility entries train the ALIGNN acquisition ranker, and generated structures are screened and ranked into a DFT-scale validation queue. The internal architecture makes the feedback gate explicit (Fig. b). A multi-agent orchestration layer coordinates the VASP-based mobility backbone across planning, execution, validation and recovery, while the runtime records the intermediate evidence needed to interpret a final mobility value.

chunks.title: InvDesMobility framework
chunks.text: A finite mobility value is therefore not sufficient by itself: the loop also records the strain points that completed, the fit quality of the deformation-potential and elastic response, the effective-mass fit, the dynamic band-edge behaviour and the channel status assigned by the reliability gate. These records allow the same numerical workflow to return a retained channel for learning, cautionary evidence for audit or a withheld channel that should not update the acquisition model. This organization follows the logic of provenance-aware high-throughput computing, in which the computational result must remain connected to the process that generated it . Here, provenance is used not only for reproducibility after the calculation, but also as an online decision variable inside the design loop. The testable claim is therefore retained feedback versus finite-but-ungated numerical output: only retained channels are admitted into the learning loop. Table summarizes the resulting guardrails in compact form, and detailed implementation choices are provided in Methods and Supplementary Notes 2-4. table

chunks.title: Mobility-feedback database
chunks.text: We first use the mobility engine to construct a seed database. Starting from 516 two-dimensional semiconductor candidates screened from 2DMatPedia , the engine evaluates four in-plane transport channels for each material: electron-x, electron-y, hole-x and hole-y. This produces 2,064 possible first-principles mobility channels, of which 573 channels, or 27.8\ This step turns a heterogeneous two-dimensional materials collection into a reusable first-principles transport resource rather than a generator input alone. In the deformation-potential protocol, a retained channel depends on band-edge identity, effective masses, strain-dependent band-edge shifts, two-dimensional elastic response and fitted deformation potentials . A finite mobility value can still be unsuitable for learning if the band edge switches under strain or the fits are poorly constrained. The database therefore stores both the value and the evidence that determines whether the value can become feedback. Channel outcomes define the material-level classes shown in Fig. a.

chunks.title: Mobility-feedback database
chunks.text: A material is QC-passed if at least one channel is retained, caution-level if it has caution-level but no retained channels, and not retained otherwise. This rule yields 280 QC-passed materials, 83 caution-level records and 153 not-retained records among the 516 seed structures. Thus, QC-passed does not mean high mobility; it means that at least one carrier-direction channel is reliable enough to enter the main analysis and feedback set. This distinction is essential for anisotropic two-dimensional semiconductors, where different carrier-direction channels can have different effective masses, deformation-potential slopes and fit stability . The retained part of the database contains 573 channel-resolved mobility entries, divided into 169 electron-x, 131 electron-y, 131 hole-x and 142 hole-y channels (Fig. b). The non-retained evidence is also kept in the audit records: 301 seed channels are caution-level, 1,020 are weak and 170 are failed or non-usable. The remaining records are therefore not hidden; they define the boundary between numerical output and feedback admitted to the learning loop.

chunks.title: Mobility-feedback database
chunks.text: This database-level distinction is what prevents large but physically fragile mobility values from being silently promoted into training data. The retained seed entries span several orders of magnitude, motivating logarithmic statistics and the material-level acquisition target log10 best retained mobility. Representative high-mobility retained electron channels include Be_3C, AgBrO_4, Ta_2O_5 and TaF_5, whereas representative high-mobility retained hole channels include GeTe, GaN, SiSe and PbS (Fig. c,d). The database supplies the two starting points for closed-loop design: QC-passed relaxed structures for generator adaptation and retained mobility entries for acquisition-ranker training.

chunks.title: Acquisition ranking
chunks.text: We next test whether the retained seed entries can guide candidate selection before expensive validation. ALIGNN provides queue-level enrichment rather than stand-alone mobility prediction: final mobility feedback comes from the first-principles validation engine, and the model is used only to prioritize DFT validation queues. The target is the material-level log10 best retained mobility, defined as the largest retained channel mobility within each QC-passed seed material. A three-repeat, five-fold cross-validation grouped by reduced formula produces 840 out-of-fold predictions for 280 materials without formula-group leakage (Fig. d-f and Supplementary Table S5). The validation results show a moderate but useful acquisition signal. The out-of-fold rank correlations are Spearman =0.393 and Kendall =0.269, with MAE = 0.679 and RMSE = 0.920 in log10 mobility units. The absolute errors are too large for surrogate discovery, but the rank information prioritizes a small validation queue. chunks.title: Generation and screening
chunks.text: We then couple acquisition ranking to feedback-updated structure generation. Figure a shows how a large generated pool is filtered into a DFT-scale validation queue. The pipeline removes duplicate and reference-like structures, then applies orthorhombic/strict-90-degree structural filtering, semiconductor screening, formation-energy filtering, dynamical-stability screening, post-phonon orthorhombic checking and mobility-guided acquisition (Supplementary Note 5). Inexpensive structural, electronic and stability screens therefore define a plausible candidate set before the mobility ranker chooses a DFT-scale queue. In this representative batch, the pool is reduced from 100,000 generated structures to 11,298 unique candidates, 1,572 orthorhombic candidates, 363 semiconducting candidates, 354 formation-pass candidates, 15 phonon-stable candidates and 13 post-phonon orthorhombic candidates. The largest reduction occurs at the dynamical-stability step: the formation-energy screen passes 354 of 363 semiconducting candidates, whereas phonon screening leaves only 15 stable candidates (Fig. b).

chunks.title: Generation and screening
chunks.text: ALIGNN then ranks the 13 surviving candidates and selects the top 10 for first-principles validation (Fig. c). Thus, the high-throughput part of the workflow creates a physically plausible DFT-scale queue; it does not assign the discovery label. This funnel clarifies the division of labour between generation and validation. The generator explores a broad structural space under feedback from retained seed and previous-loop structures, the physical filters remove invalid candidates, and the acquisition ranker operates only on candidates plausible enough to justify expensive transport validation.

chunks.title: Closed-loop validation
chunks.text: We then applied this screening-and-validation contract across the full multi-round campaign. Generated candidates are not accepted at the acquisition stage. Each selected candidate is submitted to the same first-principles mobility validation engine used for the seed database, and a generated formula enters the retained feedback set only if the workflow completes and at least one carrier-direction channel passes the final reliability gate. A representative top-k audit is shown in Supplementary Fig. S3, and the full multi-round validation provenance is supplied in Supplementary Data 4-15. At campaign scale, the loop generated 2.4 million structures and selected 102 candidates for first-principles validation under the same screening and acquisition protocol. The validation engine retained 41 generated follow-up formulas and 86 reliability-gated generated channels, expanding the retained mobility-feedback set from 573 seed channels to 659 total retained channels (Table ; Fig. ).

chunks.title: Closed-loop validation
chunks.text: Feedback accounting is chronological: only seed feedback and retained outputs from earlier completed iterations are available when a new acquisition state is built. Current-iteration DFT outcomes are admitted only after passing the validation gate, so the campaign remains a sequence of closed feedback episodes rather than a retrospective screen. These cumulative yields show why closed-loop mobility design requires conservative feedback accounting. The generator and ranker can enrich the validation queue, but the reliability gate decides which completed carrier-direction channels are usable as feedback. table

chunks.title: Reliability-gated generated candidates
chunks.text: Among the generated structures admitted by first-principles validation, the ten strongest retained formulas provide a compact view of the reliability-gated follow-up output (Fig. ). Together, these ten formulas contain 25 retained carrier-direction channels and form the high-mobility subset of the 41 retained generated formulas and 86 reliability-gated generated channels reported above. Figure a records the validation and feedback status of these ten generated formulas, and Fig. b reports their retained carrier-direction mobilities. The heatmap shows that retained feedback is channel-resolved: some formulas retain several electron and hole channels, whereas others contribute only one carrier type or one in-plane direction. Figure c compares these retained generated channels with the original retained seed-channel distributions. The strongest generated electron channels occur in Ga_4Te_2O_12 and Zr_2Ge_2S_6. Ga_4Te_2O_12 retains four reliability-gated channels, including an electron-x mobility of approximately 2.8 10^4 cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹\ and an electron-y mobility of approximately 3.4 10^3 cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹.

chunks.title: Discussion
chunks.text: InvDesMobility shows that first-principles validation can be brought into an inverse-design loop as an auditable feedback process rather than a manually curated post-generation step. The work has three connected outcomes: a first-principles mobility-feedback database for 516 two-dimensional semiconductors, a multi-agent closed-loop framework that separates generation, acquisition and validation, and generated follow-up candidates returned through the same validation gate. At campaign scale, 2.4 million generated structures are screened to 102 first-principles validation candidates, yielding 41 retained generated formulas and 86 reliability-gated generated channels. Together with the 573 retained seed channels, the campaign expands the retained mobility-feedback set to 659 carrier-direction channels. The need for this evidence is specific to the physics of the target property. Mobility depends on band curvature, strain response, elastic stiffness, band-edge identity and fitting reliability.

chunks.title: Discussion
chunks.text: A generator can expand the structural search space, and an acquisition model can enrich a small validation queue, but neither solves the feedback-admission problem by itself. InvDesMobility places this assembled quantity under explicit feedback control, connecting generative materials design with autonomous, provenance-aware and retrieval-supported scientific workflows . The role of the multi-agent architecture is orchestration rather than physical substitution. It does not make a deformation-potential calculation more fundamental, nor does it turn acquisition scores into transport results. Instead, it coordinates a multi-stage VASP-based mobility workflow across planning, execution, validation, recovery, retrieval-supported decision support and provenance recording so that only qualified first-principles outcomes become learning signals. The main practical consequence is a strict separation of roles inside the loop. Relaxed structures update the generator, retained channel entries update the acquisition ranker, acquisition scores prioritize DFT calculations and the first-principles reliability gate assigns final feedback status.

chunks.title: Discussion
chunks.text: This separation prevents surrogate scores from being interpreted as discoveries and prevents weak numerical outputs from becoming positive feedback. It also makes unsuccessful or withheld calculations informative: a completed workflow that fails the reliability gate remains part of the audit trail, even though it is not admitted as a retained channel. The channel-level formulation is more faithful to 2D transport than a single material-level mobility number. A candidate may have a reliable hole channel but an unreliable electron channel; another may have finite mobilities in both in-plane directions but only one direction supported by stable strain and effective-mass fits. Collapsing the workflow to a best mobility would overstate what has been learned, whereas rejecting the whole material would discard useful information. Channel-wise feedback keeps the usable part of the calculation without promoting unsupported channels.

chunks.title: Discussion
chunks.text: The present study does not provide an agent-versus-script comparison on identical candidates, and we do not claim that the control layer changes first-principles values relative to an ideal scripted implementation of the same physical contracts. The supported comparison is ungated numerical output versus quality-controlled retained feedback. In the seed database, 573 of 1,894 usable channels are retained as feedback; admitting every finite or usable value would therefore return many weak or caution-level channels to the learning loop. This conservative policy trades apparent yield for feedback integrity, which is especially important because an incorrect positive feedback entry can influence later candidate generation and acquisition. The acquisition results should be interpreted in the same way. ALIGNN is useful here because it enriches a small DFT validation queue for high-mobility candidates, not because it predicts final mobilities with the precision needed for stand-alone discovery claims. The retained seed channels are also consistent with external scale checks that were not used for training, ranking or quality assignment.

chunks.title: Discussion
chunks.text: The main calculation is non-spin-polarized and does not include DFT+U or spin-orbit coupling. Defects, substrate effects, contacts, grain boundaries, polar optical scattering and finite-temperature anharmonicity are also outside the main calculation. These boundaries are particularly important for rare-earth candidates, where localized 4f states, magnetic order and spin-orbit coupling may change band-edge character and retained mobility channels. Rare-earth generated candidates therefore require spin-polarized DFT+U and spin-orbit robustness checks before stronger material-level claims are made. Several limitations also arise from the closed-loop strategy itself. The generator is updated with QC-passed relaxed structures, while mobility values are routed to the acquisition ranker rather than used as direct generator targets. This design reduces the risk of overfitting the generator to a small and noisy mobility-feedback set, but it also means that structural exploration and mobility optimization are only indirectly coupled.

chunks.title: Discussion
chunks.text: The acquisition ranker is trained on 280 QC-passed seed materials, which is sufficient for enrichment but not for broad extrapolative prediction over all 2D chemistries. Finally, the strict orthorhombic and 90-degree filters make the present campaign well aligned with the deformation-potential protocol used here, but they exclude potentially interesting lower-symmetry 2D semiconductors. Future work can improve both the physics and the loop strategy. More complete transport workflows could incorporate electron-phonon scattering, spin-orbit coupling, DFT+U, magnetic order or defect-limited transport for narrower candidate sets. The acquisition model could be made uncertainty-aware and multi-objective, balancing mobility, stability, synthesizability and novelty, and the generator could be conditioned on reliability-aware feedback from both successes and failures. More generally, the same feedback architecture should apply to other expensive, multi-stage first-principles property evaluations, such as thermal conductivity, defect tolerance, excitonic response, catalytic activity and phonon stability.

chunks.title: Methods
chunks.text: InvDesMobility was implemented as a reproducible closed-loop campaign rather than as a single screening script. The methods below follow the same order as the Results: seed data definition, runtime policy, deterministic first-principles mobility calculation, reliability assessment, generation and acquisition, acquisition-ranker validation and round-wise feedback accounting. All reported mobility values were produced by deterministic calculations and entered the feedback set only through the reliability rules described below. The methodological goal was to make each feedback decision reproducible from stored records. The workflow therefore records material identity, structure source, calculation status, fitted physical quantities, uncertainty estimates, quality labels, acquisition scores and round-wise feedback state as separate fields. Figures and tables are derived from these records rather than from manually edited candidate lists. This design makes the main comparison explicit: unqualified numerical output is not the same object as retained feedback.

chunks.title: Seed dataset and channel definitions
chunks.text: Seed structures were selected from 2DMatPedia using a 2D semiconductor pre-screening procedure . The database provides a bottom-up and top-down reference pool for 2D materials and is complementary to other high-throughput 2D-materials resources . After structural and electronic filtering, 516 candidates were passed to the mobility feedback engine. For each material, four in-plane transport channels were defined: electron-x, electron-y, hole-x and hole-y. The x and y directions were assigned from standardized in-plane lattice vectors and used consistently for seed and generated structures. The channel was the basic unit of mobility feedback throughout the study. A material-level target was used only when training or evaluating the acquisition ranker; in that case, the target was the best retained channel mobility for a material after applying the reliability gate. Materials without at least one retained channel were excluded from the acquisition-ranker training target but remained in the audit records. Full seed records, channel records and material-level labels are provided in Supplementary Data 1-3.

chunks.title: Runtime architecture and control policy
chunks.text: The multi-agent mobility framework is organized around a typed shared state that links workflow planning, tool execution, validation, recovery and feedback assignment to the same VASP-based mobility backbone. The orchestration layer uses a typed state graph with persistent checkpointing, structured tool outputs, recovery and validation records, VASP-native tool calls and a common result schema. In batch operation, the framework claims candidates from a validation queue, prepares VASP inputs, invokes the same single-material runner used for individual calculations and records completed, failed or skipped outcomes in the shared schema. This design follows the same motivation as provenance-aware workflow systems: every output should be traceable to a concrete computational state and execution path . The retrieval-supported policy layer provides stage-scoped context for VASP-writing stages, including relaxation, SCF, band-structure and strain-loop substages. Within these stages, it can propose INCAR or KPOINTS adjustments and recovery actions .

chunks.title: First-principles mobility workflow
chunks.text: All main-workflow first-principles mobility calculations used VASP with the projector augmented-wave method and the PBE exchange-correlation functional . Calculations were non-spin-polarized and did not include spin-orbit coupling unless explicitly stated for follow-up analysis. PBE PAW potentials were used. 2D structures were treated as slab systems with one k point along the out-of-plane direction. Unless otherwise stated, ENCUT was 600 eV, ISMEAR = 0, SIGMA = 0.01 eV, ALGO = Normal, NELM = 300, NELMIN = 4 and IVDW = 12 . Relaxations used EDIFF = 10^-5 eV, EDIFFG = -0.01 eV ^-1, IBRION = 2, POTIM = 0.5 and NSW = 200. SCF, band and effective-mass stages used EDIFF = 10^-6 eV. Band structures were evaluated along -X-S-Y- with 40 points per segment. Stage-specific KPOINTS policies and slab settings were handled by the workflow configuration and recorded in the calculation provenance, so the reported mobility entries can be traced back to their exact VASP input state rather than to manually edited labels. The workflow order was fixed for all main calculations.

chunks.title: First-principles mobility workflow
chunks.text: Each candidate was first relaxed, then evaluated by static self-consistent and band-structure calculations. Effective masses were extracted near the relevant band edges, after which uniaxial strain calculations were performed along the two in-plane directions. Deformation-potential slopes and 2D elastic constants were obtained from these strain series. Mobility was assembled only after all required intermediate quantities were available for the corresponding channel. Carrier mobility was evaluated using the 2D deformation-potential-limited expression equation _c, = e ^3 C_ ^2Dk_ BT\,m^*_c, m_c,dE_1,c, ^2, equation where c denotes carrier type, denotes transport direction, C_ ^2D is the 2D elastic constant, m^*_c, is the transport effective mass, m_c,d is the density-of-states effective mass and E_1,c, is the deformation-potential constant. Mobilities were evaluated at 300 K. Effective masses were fitted from 21 points with 0.01 ^-1 spacing within |k-k_0| 0.03 ^-1. Deformation-potential and elastic fits used uniaxial strains from -0.020 to 0.020 in steps of 0.005, with band-edge energies aligned to the vacuum level before fitting.

chunks.title: Reliability assessment
chunks.text: Reliability was assigned at the carrier-direction channel level before any record was used for training or acquisition feedback. Seed channels were retained if they had completed workflow status, positive finite mobility, finite E_1 and C^2D, at least seven completed strain points, (R^2_E_1,R^2_C^2D) 0.985, relative uncertainty of E_1 0.25, relative uncertainty of C^2D 0.10, |E_1| 0.10 eV, effective-mass fit R^2 0.95 and effective mass between 0.02m_0 and 20m_0. Caution-level seed channels used weaker thresholds, including at least five strain points, (R^2_E_1,R^2_C^2D) 0.95, relative uncertainty of E_1 0.50, relative uncertainty of C^2D 0.20 and |E_1| 0.05 eV. Generated channels were retained under the final feedback rule only when the workflow completed, mobility was positive and finite, key fitted quantities were finite, fitting checks passed, effective mass was accepted and no dynamic band-edge switch was detected.

chunks.title: Generation, screening and acquisition
chunks.text: Structure generation used DiffCSP, following the InvDesFlow implementation . The model was fine-tuned with QC-passed relaxed structures during feedback updates, while mobility values were not used as direct generator targets. Generator updates used only feedback available before the corresponding generation round; current-round validation outcomes were excluded until the round closed. Generated structures were passed through a staged physical-screening pipeline before mobility acquisition ranking. This pipeline includes duplicate removal, orthorhombic/strict-90-degree filtering, ALIGNN electronic screening, MEGNet formation-energy screening, PhononBench dynamical-stability screening, post-phonon orthorhombic consistency checking and ALIGNN mobility acquisition ranking . Duplicate removal used lattice tolerance 0.2, site tolerance 0.3 and angle tolerance 5.0^ with pymatgen . The formation-energy threshold was <0.0 eV atom^-1, and the phonon-stability workflow used a 2 2 1 supercell.

chunks.text: The ranker was applied only after these filters, ensuring that acquisition scores selected among plausible validation candidates rather than replacing the physical screens. A generation batch can sample 100,000 candidate structures. chunks.title: ALIGNN acquisition-ranker validation
chunks.text: The ALIGNN mobility model was evaluated as an acquisition ranker, not as a final mobility predictor (Fig. d-f). Top-decile enrichment reports the fraction of true top-decile seed materials recovered within predicted top-ranked fractions.

chunks.title: Round-wise feedback accounting
chunks.text: Feedback accounting was performed round by round to avoid leakage from current-loop validation results into current-loop acquisition. For loop N, before-round feedback counts are the seed retained channels and structures plus retained generated feedback from loops earlier than N. Current-loop validation results are counted only after the loop completes. Runtime manifest counts are reported separately as audit metadata and are not used to define retained feedback. Two counts were therefore maintained for each round. The first count describes the validation queue and includes submitted, completed, failed and skipped first-principles jobs. The second count describes feedback admitted to the learning loop and includes only retained formulas and retained carrier-direction channels. Keeping these counts separate prevents completed but non-retained numerical outputs from being mistaken for successful feedback and ensures that the cumulative label count corresponds to the actual training signal available after each round.

chunks.title: Supplementary Note 1: Seed records and channel definitions
chunks.text: The seed set contains 516 2DMatPedia-derived two-dimensional semiconductor candidates after structural and electronic pre-screening. chunks.title: Supplementary Note 2: Implementation modules and reproducibility boundaries
chunks.text: The implementation is organized into three functional code modules that match the architecture in Fig. 1 rather than the narrative of the Results section. The first module is the stateful first-principles mobility runtime, which executes single-material and batch mobility calculations, stores typed workflow state, tracks calculation artifacts and records validation outcomes. The second module is the generation, screening and acquisition pipeline, which builds mobility seed and feedback datasets, adapts the DiffCSP/InvDesFlow generator, generates candidate structures, deduplicates candidates, applies physical screens, ranks survivors with ALIGNN and exports strict-90-degree top-k validation queues. The third module is the campaign bridge, which extracts trusted feedback from completed mobility batches, archives trusted relaxed structures, builds feedback-aware DiffCSP and ALIGNN datasets and launches the next validation round. This modular split is used for reproducibility and audit, not as a scientific claim in itself.

chunks.title: Supplementary Note 5: Generation and physical screening pipeline
chunks.text: The generation/screening route is: DiffCSP/InvDesFlow generation; generated-set self-deduplication and deduplication against the 516 seed/reference structures; orthorhombic or strict-90-degree filtering; ALIGNN electronic screening; MEGNet formation-energy prediction and filtering at E_form<0 eV atom^-1; PhononBench dynamical-stability screening; post-phonon strict-90-degree validation; ALIGNN mobility ranking; and top-k CIF export. The PhononBench workflow performs relaxation, phonopy displacement-supercell construction, force-constant assembly and phonon-spectrum analysis. The phonon-stability gate is the dominant physical filtering step in the feedback-updated generation round.

chunks.title: Supplementary Note 6: Generated-candidate validation provenance
chunks.text: The representative top-k validation map in Supplementary Fig. S3 is retained as a provenance example because it shows the separation between ALIGNN acquisition and first-principles label assignment. The updated source-data package reports the full multi-round generated-candidate audit after relaxed-structure deduplication: 106 raw VASP workflow rows are reduced to 102 representative submitted candidates, yielding 41 retained generated formulas and 86 trusted generated carrier-direction channels. Candidate-level validation outcomes, retained channel-resolved mobility values, rejected-feedback records and duplicate-structure clusters are provided in Supplementary Data 4-15. The multi-round accounting tables in Supplementary Data 25-27 then connect these validation records to the chronological feedback state used by the loop.

chunks.title: Supplementary Note 7: Reliability-gating and literature sanity checks
chunks.text: The current data do not provide a same-candidate pure-script versus agentic-runtime ablation. Instead, the available retrospective control is a reliability-gating audit: how many finite or otherwise usable mobility outputs would have entered feedback without channel-level quality control. Supplementary Table S8 reports this ungated-output comparison. Literature sanity-check records are provided in Supplementary Table S9 and Supplementary Data 30. These records were not used for training, acquisition ranking or quality assignment.

chunks.title: Supplementary Note 8: Rare-earth candidate follow-up
chunks.text: The main high-throughput validation workflow uses a non-spin-polarized, no-SOC PBE deformation-potential protocol. Rare-earth candidates retained by this protocol require higher-level follow-up because localized 4f states and spin-orbit coupling may alter band-edge character and transport. Sm_2Se_2I_2 is therefore treated as a retained rare-earth candidate under the main validation protocol rather than as a definitive final material claim. Supplementary Fig. S4 shows a spin-polarized PBE+U band-structure check as an example follow-up analysis, and Supplementary Fig. S5 reports the main-workflow band structures for the ten highlighted generated candidates.

supported: Campaign counts connect seed materials, generated candidates, DFT validation, and retained feedback labels.

unsupported: Displayed values are stored outputs from the manuscript workflow, not calculations launched in the browser.
Q&A answers are grounded in retrieved manuscript passages; source data and figures remain the authoritative evidence.
ALIGNN is interpreted as an acquisition ranker; final mobility evidence comes from first-principles validation and reliability gates.
Generated materials are computational follow-up candidates; experimental, device, and synthesizability claims require additional work.
Full electron-phonon transport and rare-earth robustness checks belong to narrower follow-up studies.
